newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SWIMMING-DISQUALIFICATION DENIES VOELKER RARE DOUBLE.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-DISQUALIFICATION DENIES VOELKER RARE DOUBLE.

text.p: Sandra Voelker was denied a rare golden double at the world short-course swimming championships on Friday when she was disqualified after touching first in the 100 metres backstroke final.
The German, who had earlier won the 50 metres freestyle crown, led throughout the backstroke and touched at the finish 0.25 seconds ahead of China's Lu Donghua, the fastest qualifier.
But Voelker's joy was short-lived because officials disqualified her for swimming under water more than the 15 metres allowed after the start.
The decision gave China a one-two, with Lu first in 59.75 seconds and Chen Yan second in one minute 0.14 seconds.
Defending champion Misty Hyman, third in Thursday's 200 butterfly, found herself on the podium again, having been promoted from fourth to third in 1:00.17.
